ask: Just a shell for an HR onboarding portal: nav with 6 sections, and only the 'First day checklist' page built properly. It's for a stakeholder walkthrough tomorrow morning.
notes: The person states the depth: a shell plus one page in full. A default of 'every module in full' goes against their words. The six section names are open and fair to draft as a default.
message:
**Goal:** a clickable shell of an HR onboarding portal. The nav has 6 sections, and only "First day checklist" is built properly, for tomorrow morning's stakeholder walkthrough.

**Found:**
- Ask: 6 nav sections, one built in full, the other five are shell pages (from your message)
- Ask: shown to stakeholders tomorrow morning, so it must run without surprises (from your message)
- Ask: only "First day checklist" is named; the other five names are mine (from your message)
- Working folder: empty, so this is a new product in `./hr-onboarding-portal/` (from the folder)
- Look: no logo, colours or fonts anywhere, so the plain look is used (from the folder)
- Browser: chrome-headless-shell, so every click is checked for real (start check)

**Track:** full, because you will show it to stakeholders. This adds 3 name and logo options on the real header, and a link for every state of the checklist (empty, all done, one task opened).

Coverage: 4 clear · partial: Who and their job, Data and facts, Edge cases · missing: Look, Done signal

**Done means:**
- Nav shows 6 sections; each opens its own page, none blank
- First day checklist is complete: tasks, tick-off, progress, empty state
- The other 5 pages are titled shell pages, not built
- Every link opens and every click works in a real browser
- A fresh reviewer says PASS with no P1

About 90 minutes and 5 helper agents, within a budget of 120 minutes.

1. What are the other 5 sections called?
   Recommended: Documents, Equipment and access, Meet your team, Benefits, Training.
   Why it matters: the names go on the nav your stakeholders will read.

2. Who is on the page, and what one job do they come to do?
   Recommended: a new hire on their first morning, who works through what to do today and ticks it off.
   Why it matters: a new hire and an HR admin need different checklist pages.

3. What does a task on the First day checklist hold, and what happens when it is ticked?
   Recommended: a title, who it is with, a time, a short note; ticking moves it to done and the progress bar updates (for example "3 of 8 done").
   Why it matters: this is the one page built properly, so it is what they will click.

4. Is there a company name, logo or colours to use?
   Recommended: none; use the plain look and pick a working name from the 3 options.
   Why it matters: stakeholders judge a branded demo differently from a grey one.

5. Quick or full?
   Recommended: full. Quick makes every section one page and skips the name options and the state links; full adds both.
   Why it matters: full takes longer, and you have until tomorrow morning.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.

evidence.completeness: Settles shell ("the other five are shell pages"), 6 sections with proposed names, checklist contents (Q3) and persona (Q2 "a new hire on their first morning").
evidence.no_redundancy: Q5 "Quick or full?" asks how deep to go, though "Just a shell" with one page built properly already answers it.
evidence.defaults_quality: Q1-Q4 defaults are concrete and fitting (named sections, task fields, "3 of 8 done"), but Q5 defaults to "full", which adds scope the person did not want.
evidence.clarity: Five numbered questions with defaults, but a long brief plus jargon like "Coverage: 4 clear · partial: ... missing: Look, Done signal" slows a busy reader.
evidence.respects_words: "Track: full ... adds 3 name and logo options on the real header, and a link for every state" goes beyond "Just a shell" with only one page built.
evidence.overall: Solid brief and good persona/checklist defaults, but it escalates a stated shell to a full track and asks a depth question the ask already answered.
